key_insight: Instead of only adding more computation steps, Latent Lattice Language Models increase the number of active internal states. Their “Lattice of Latents” combines horizontal streams that persist across time with the usual vertical flow through model layers.
problem_solved: Language models commonly expand computation through greater depth, repeated layers, or latent reasoning steps. This work explores a different route: expanding the internal state available for processing sequences.
method: Introduce per-layer horizontal latent streams that run recurrently across sequence positions.
Maintain the vertical residual stream that carries information through model depth.
Combine these time- and depth-oriented streams into a lattice of active computational states.
impact: The approach offers practitioners an alternative architectural direction for increasing model capacity beyond depth or extra reasoning steps. The provided abstract is incomplete, so performance gains and computational trade-offs cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A two-axis lattice diagram: sequence position horizontally and model depth vertically.
Color-coded arrows distinguishing recurrent latent streams from the vertical residual stream.
A side-by-side schematic contrasting a standard residual pathway with the latent lattice.
A conceptual comparison showing more computation steps versus more active computational states.
paper_authors: Shivam Duggal, Zongze Wu, William T. Freeman, Antonio Torralba, Richard Zhang
